# CLAIMs with `tags` `databases`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Databases and data structures** — how stored data is organized so that it can be found and kept current — physical database design and index selection, materialized views and the choice of which answers to precompute, adaptive and self-organizing structures, lower bounds on lookup, caching and paging; and the cost of organizing ahead of use against organizing in use. Read for itself, not as ML practice: learned indexes and other machine-learning approaches go to the anthology (ADR-045).

| [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) | "If I can't find it, it isn't there" | The medic's "If I can't find it, it isn't there" ([CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)) and the owner's "if I can't find it quickly enough, it may as well not be there" ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) act on a failed search as if it showed absence. One find shows presence, but absence needs a check of everything, which a deadline forbids. First filed as negation as failure on a time bound, with Reiter and Clark unread. Both readings corrected it. The two assumptions are separate. Reiter's closed-world assumption is that the database is complete about the world. Clark's negation as failure is licensed only by finite failure: "the exhaustive but unsuccessful search for a proof". A search cut off by a deadline meets neither, so the rule is stronger than both. It assumes a closed world and that the unsearched part would have failed. It is safe when the full pass finishes in time. In [CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md) the EMT knew the drug was stocked, which is exactly where Reiter shows the closed-world assumption inconsistent. So there it was a decision to stop, not an inference. | Superseded — by [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) |

| [CLAIM-313](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-313.md) v2 | With copies, overlapping partitions coexist | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on locality-sensitive hashing (Indyk and Motwani 1998; Andoni, Laarhoven, Razenshteyn and Waingarten 2017) set against [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md)'s premise that "a set of k bins realizes one partition of the collection at a time".
